prompt: I use a wheelchair and we're staying near Zion for three days. Help me plan something scenic without assuming hiking.
response: For three days at Zion, I’d build the scenery around wheelchair-accessible buildings and the museum’s viewing patio rather than assume you want to hike. The Kolob Canyons outing is a separate, lighter day; confirm how you’ll get between areas before committing to it.

outputs.intro: For three days at Zion, I’d build the scenery around wheelchair-accessible buildings and the museum’s viewing patio rather than assume you want to hike. The Kolob Canyons outing is a separate, lighter day; confirm how you’ll get between areas before committing to it.

days.label: Canyon orientation and the museum’s cliff views

stops.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
stops.note: Start at this wheelchair-accessible facility near the South Entrance; it has reserved parking and paved walkways. Ask about access for the rest of your visit.
stops.why: It gives you a practical start without making a trail the centerpiece.

stops.name: Zion Human History Museum
stops.note: Use the ramp to reach the accessible exhibits and park film. Check seasonal hours before going; the museum also has views of the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain outside.
stops.why: The exhibits and canyon scenery offer a substantial, flexible first-day visit.

days.label: Zion Lodge and canyon nature exhibits

stops.name: Zion Lodge
stops.note: Spend time in the wheelchair-accessible dining room and auditorium, and take a leisurely break. Confirm current access arrangements before setting out; access to the lodge is subject to shuttle restrictions.
stops.why: This makes room for an unhurried canyon day without relying on a hike.

stops.name: Zion Nature Center
stops.note: Explore the interactive exhibits via the accessible entrance ramp. It operates seasonally, so check hours for your dates before making it part of the day.
stops.why: The exhibits provide a different perspective on Zion’s habitats after time at the lodge.

alternatives.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
alternatives.note: If the Nature Center is closed, return for the accessible outdoor exhibits and a more leisurely look around.

days.label: Kolob Canyons and a final museum-patio view

stops.name: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center
stops.timeWindow: Morning, outside the noon–1 PM closure
stops.note: Use the accessible walkways, information desk, exhibits and restrooms. This is a separate park area, listed by NPS as 45 miles north of Springdale; plan your transport before setting out.
stops.why: It brings a different part of Zion into your three-day visit, without adding an unverified trail outing.

stops.name: Zion Human History Museum Patio
stops.timeWindow: Later afternoon, if the return trip leaves time
stops.note: Approach via the museum parking area for the wheelchair-accessible viewing patio overlooking West Temple and the Towers of the Virgin.
stops.why: This gives your last day a specific scenic viewpoint, rather than ending it at an information desk.

narrativeSections.markdown: The plan favors places with documented wheelchair access, but that doesn’t establish an accessible way to travel between them. Kolob Canyons is the biggest logistical commitment; if transport there isn’t workable, spend that day at the museum patio and other accessible main-canyon stops instead. Check current hours and access arrangements for your dates, especially for the seasonal Nature Center and the lodge.
